Según los factores de riesgo del informe 10-K de FY2025 de NVIDIA (Item 1A), la dependencia de fundiciones, fabricantes contratados y proveedores externos reduce su control directo principalmente sobre:

1. Cantidad de producto (product quantity).
2. Calidad del producto (product quality).
3. Calendarios y plazos de entrega (delivery schedules).

Asimismo, NVIDIA señala que esta falta de control directo abarca aspectos críticos del proceso productivo como:
- La capacidad de fabricación y testeo, así como la obtención de materias primas por parte de las fundiciones.
- La implementación y desarrollo de tecnologías de procesos avanzados y diseños de memoria.
- Los rendimientos de fabricación (manufacturing yields), sujetos a la tecnología propietaria de las fundiciones.
- El riesgo de que los subcontratistas prioricen pedidos de competidores u otros clientes, o que modifiquen componentes sin la cualificación de NVIDIA.
- La extensión imprevista de los plazos de entrega (lead times) y el aumento de costes en periodos de escasez.

Foreign Exchange Rate Risk

The Company’s exposure to foreign exchange rate risk relates primarily to the Company being a net receiver of currencies other than the U.S. dollar. Changes in exchange rates, and in particular a strengthening of the U.S. dollar, will negatively affect the Company’s net sales and gross margins as expressed in U.S. dollars. Fluctuations in exchange rates may also affect the fair values of certain of the Company’s assets and liabilities. To protect against foreign exchange rate risk, the Company may use derivative instruments, offset exposures, or adjust local currency pricing of its products and services. However, the Company may choose to not hedge certain foreign currency exposures for a variety of reasons, including accounting considerations or prohibitive cost.

The Company applied a value-at-risk (“VAR”) model to its foreign currency derivative positions to assess the potential impact of fluctuations in exchange rates. The VAR model used a Monte Carlo simulation. The VAR is the maximum expected loss in fair value, for a given confidence interval, to the Company’s foreign currency derivative positions due to adverse movements in rates. Based on the results of the model, the Company estimates, with 95% confidence, a maximum one-day loss in fair value of $538 million and $669 million as of September 28, 2024 and September 30, 2023, respectively. Changes in the Company’s underlying foreign currency exposures, which were excluded from the assessment, generally offset changes in the fair values of the Company’s foreign currency derivatives.

We allocate goodwill to reporting units based on the reporting unit expected to benefit from the business combination. Goodwill is tested for impairment at the reporting unit level (operating segment or one level below an operating segment) on an annual basis (May 1) and between annual tests if an event occurs or circumstances change that would more likely than not reduce the fair value of a reporting unit below its carrying value. These events or circumstances could include a significant change in the business climate, legal factors, operating performance indicators, competition, or sale or disposition of a significant portion of a reporting unit.

Application of the goodwill impairment test requires judgment, including the identification of reporting units, assignment of assets and liabilities to reporting units, assignment of goodwill to reporting units, and determination of the fair value of each reporting unit. The fair value of each reporting unit is estimated primarily through the use of a discounted cash flow methodology. This analysis requires significant judgments, including estimation of future cash flows, which is dependent on internal forecasts, estimation of the long-term rate of growth for our business, estimation of the useful life over which cash flows will occur, and determination of our weighted average cost of capital.

The estimates used to calculate the fair value of a reporting unit change from year to year based on operating results, market conditions, and other factors. Costs incurred internally in researching and developing a software product to be marketed or sold to external users are charged to expense until technological feasibility has been established for the product. Once technological feasibility is established, software costs are capitalized until the product is available for general release to customers. Judgment is required in determining when technological feasibility of a product is established. We have determined that technological feasibility for our software products is reached after all high-risk development issues have been resolved through coding and testing. Executive Overview of Full Year 2024 Results

Our mission is to build the future of human connection and the technology that makes it possible.

Our financial results and key Family metrics for 2024 are set forth below. Total revenue for 2024 was $164.50 billion, an increase of 22% compared to 2023, due to an increase in advertising revenue. Revenue on a constant currency basis would have increased 23% compared to 2023. Ad impressions delivered across our Family of Apps in 2024 increased 11% year-over-year, and our average price per ad increased 10% year-over-year.

Income from operations for 2024 was $69.38 billion, an increase of $22.63 billion, or 48%, compared to 2023, driven by an increase in advertising revenue, partially offset by an increase in costs and expenses. The increase in costs and expenses was mainly due to increases in operational expenses related to our data centers and technical infrastructure and employee compensation, partially offset by lower restructuring and legal-related costs.

---

[META-2024-7-0022] META FY2024 Item 7 (similitud 0.784)
Advertising

Advertising revenue in 2024 increased $28.68 billion, or 22%, compared to 2023 due to increases in ad impressions delivered and average price per ad. In 2024, ad impressions delivered increased by 11%, as compared with a 28% increase in 2023, year-over-year. Ad impressions delivered during 2024 grew in all regions, especially in Asia-Pacific and Rest of World, which was mostly driven by increases in users and their engagement on our products. In 2024, the average price per ad increased by 10%, as compared with a decrease of 9% in 2023, year-over-year. The increase in average price per ad in 2024 was driven by an increase in advertising demand, which we believe is mainly due to ongoing improvements to our ad performance from our ad targeting and measurement tools. This increase was partially offset by a higher number of ad impressions delivered, especially in geographies and in products, such as Reels, that monetize at lower rates. Other factors are discussed in the section entitled "—Executive Overview of Full Year 2024 Results." In addition, the online commerce vertical was the largest contributor to the increase in advertising revenue in 2024 compared to 2023. We anticipate that future advertising revenue will be driven by a combination of price and ad impressions delivered.

Other revenue

FoA other revenue in 2024 increased $664 million, or 63%, compared to 2023. The increase was primarily driven by WhatsApp Business Platform revenue.

Reality Labs

RL revenue in 2024 increased $250 million, or 13%, compared to 2023. The increase was mostly due to an increase in RL consumer hardware products sold.

Esto representa una variación absoluta positiva de +13.896.000.000 USD (+13.896 millones de dólares), equivalente a un incremento del +20,03% (+20%).

Comparativa de los factores que explican el aumento de costes y gastos en cada informe:

1. Informe 10-K de FY2024 (comparativa 2024 vs. 2023):
- Causas principales generales: El aumento en costes y gastos se debió principalmente a mayores gastos operativos vinculados a centros de datos e infraestructura técnica (sobre todo mayor gasto de depreciación) y a mayores costes de compensación a empleados (por un aumento del 13% en la plantilla de ingeniería y funciones técnicas) [META-2024-7-0001, META-2024-7-0024].
- Factores compensatorios a la baja: Estos aumentos fueron parcialmente compensados por menores costes de reestructuración (tras el plan del año previo) y un impacto favorable de 1.550 millones de USD en gastos legales acumulados, lo que redujo los gastos generales y administrativos (G&A, -15%) y de ventas y marketing (-8%) [META-2024-7-0024, META-2024-7-0025].

2. Informe 10-K de FY2025 (comparativa 2025 vs. 2024):
- Causas principales generales: El incremento de costes y gastos fue impulsado de nuevo por mayores gastos de compensación laboral y costes de infraestructura [META-2025-7-0001].
- Especificidades de FY2025:
  * I+D (+31%): Mayor compensación al personal (aumento del 8% en el número de empleados técnicos y de ingeniería, así como mayor compensación basada en acciones) y mayores costes de infraestructura destinados a I+D, destacando expresamente las iniciativas de inteligencia artificial (IA) [META-2025-7-0024].
  * Coste de ingresos (+20%): Mayores gastos operativos de infraestructura técnica y centros de datos, aunque con una desaceleración en el ritmo de crecimiento de la depreciación gracias a la extensión de la vida útil estimada de servidores y activos de red desde el 1 de enero de 2025, junto con mayores costes por acuerdos de distribución/socios [META-2025-7-0024].
  * G&A (+25%): Aumento de costes legales, impulsado principalmente por el efecto comparativo ('lapping') de la reducción de 1.550 millones de USD en provisiones legales de la que se había beneficiado el ejercicio anterior [META-2025-7-0025].
  * Reality Labs: Aumento de costes por compensación, desarrollo tecnológico y pérdidas estimadas en compromisos de compra no cancelables de inventario [META-2025-7-0026].

3. Contraste entre ambos ejercicios:
Mientras que en ambos años el crecimiento de la plantilla técnica y la inversión en infraestructura fueron los motores estructurales de coste, en FY2024 la depreciación se aceleró fuertemente y los costes legales/reestructuración actuaron como mitigadores a la baja; en cambio, en FY2025 el gasto en infraestructura estuvo fuertemente marcado por la aceleración en IA, el crecimiento de la depreciación se moderó contablemente por la extensión de la vida útil de los activos, y los costes legales volvieron a subir al desaparecer el beneficio extraordinario de 2024.
